question_text:
(a) Calculate the number of free electrons per cubic meter for silver, assuming that there are 1.3 free electrons per silver atom. The electrical conductivity and density for Ag are $6.8 \times 10^{7}(\Omega \cdot m)^{-1}$ and $10.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, respectively. The atomic weight of Ag is $107.87 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$.
(b) Now compute the electron mobility for Ag.

Give your answer as a tuple (the number of free electrons in (a), the electron mobility for Ag in (b)).The units of each required answer are (m^-3, m^2/Vs), respectively.
response:
## Step-by-step Reasoning

### (a) Number of free electrons per m³

Convert density to SI:
$$\rho = 10.5\;\text{g/cm}^3 = 10.5\times10^{6}\;\text{g/m}^3$$

Number of Ag atoms per m³:
$$n_{\text{atoms}} = \frac{\rho}{A}\,N_A = \frac{10.5\times10^{6}}{107.87}(6.022\times10^{23})$$

With 1.3 free electrons per atom:
$$n = 1.3\,n_{\text{atoms}} \approx 7.62\times10^{28}\;\text{m}^{-3}$$

### (b) Electron mobility

Using $\sigma = n|e|\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{\sigma}{n|e|} = \frac{6.8\times10^{7}}{(7.62\times10^{28})(1.602\times10^{-19})} \approx 5.57\times10^{-3}\;\text{m}^2/\text{V·s}$$

$$\boxed{(7.62\times10^{28},\; 5.57\times10^{-3})}$$
